New Hope to Buy Out Malabar, Create Combined Mining Group Worth $4.4 Billion
By Stuart Condie
SYDNEY--Australian coal miner New Hope agreed to take full ownership of closely held Malabar Resources in an all-scrip deal that would create a group with a US$4.4 billion market capitalization.
New Hope on Monday said it would give half a new share for each Malabar share, giving the smaller miner an implied equity value of 1.8 billion Australian dollars, or US$1.25 billion.
Shares in New Hope were valued at A$5.84 each ahead of Monday's open.
New Hope already owns 26% of Malabar, which is ramping up the Maxwell underground mine in Australia's New South Wales state. The mine will mostly produce coal for steelmaking.
New Hope has progressively raised its stake over recent years, including as recently as a year ago.
New Hope said the boards of both companies unanimously recommended the transaction. It expects completion by March 2027, it added.

"This transaction provides a clear pathway to unlock the full value of the Maxwell Mine for both shareholder groups," New Hope Chief Executive Rob Bishop said. "The combination strengthens our production platform, enhances future growth opportunities, and creates an opportunity to realise synergies in operations, logistics, financing, marketing and corporate functions."
